gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the 70mai M310's "2K QHD" is 2304×1296 (2.99 MP), which is 1.44× the pixels of 1080p and not the "1.5 times" 70mai claims, and 19% fewer pixels than the 2560×1440 that DashCamTalk's price tracker labels it as.
standout_why: Compared against Auto Roamer (cited), Guidespot (cited) and DashCamTalk's price tracker (cited); Dash & Drive (cited) could not be opened (certificate error), so it is unchecked. Auto Roamer already gives the M310's 2304×1296 at 30 fps, SC3336P sensor, 300 mAh lithium battery, 256 GB card limit and separately sold hardwire kit, so the raw specs are not new. What the pages I read lack: the pixel arithmetic against 1080p and 1440p, any note that the tracker's "2K (1440p)" label disagrees with 70mai's own page, a hardwire-kit price, and the fact that 70mai's US page for the M310 Plus 4K names no sensor and no frame rate. The half that would decide the pick (the DDPAI N2's 2560×1440 and supercapacitor against the M310) I could not open on a DDPAI page, so the standout stays at 1.
decides: It confirms the 70mai M310 as a safe front-only pick but shows its "2K" is the smallest one on sale: 2304×1296 with a lithium battery. If DDPAI's page confirms the N2 Front as 2560×1440 at 30 fps with a supercapacitor, the N2 Front (1-channel, $49.00 in the brief's 2026-11-21 store read) wins on pixels and heat and is linkable through awin:ddpai. The $49 N2 is front only; the N2 Dual (front + rear) is $89.00 in the same read, so ChatGPT's "best front + rear" label at $49 is wrong on the brief's figures. None of the five dash cams we already link is under $50, so the page needs a new record for a DDPAI under-$50 model (N2 Front, MINIPRO 2K at $39.00, MINI PRO 3K or MINI2X 2026 at $49.00) or it must skip. Before publishing, someone must open the DDPAI store page for specs; it returned HTTP 429 on every attempt today.

findings.label: Channels, resolution and frame rate behind the "2K QHD" label
findings.note: Maker's global product page; the US subdomain us.70mai.com did not resolve. The page heads the section "2K QHD" and calls the sensor "3-megapixel".

findings.label: "2K" normalised to pixel count
findings.value: 2,985,984 pixels (2.99 MP): 1.44× the pixels of 1080p, 1.2× the lines, 81% of 2560×1440
findings.note: Arithmetic on the maker's figure: 2304×1296 = 2,985,984; 1920×1080 = 2,073,600 (ratio 1.44); 2560×1440 = 3,686,400 (ratio 0.81; 1440p has 23.5% more pixels). 70mai's page says "1.5 times clearer than standard 1080P".

findings.label: Image sensor named by the maker
findings.value: SC3336P; aperture F2.0; field of view 130°
findings.note: The page does not say whether 130° is diagonal or horizontal. Guidespot lists "130-140 Degree" for the same camera.

findings.label: Power backup (heat)
findings.note: Maker's spec list. The page states no operating temperature.

findings.label: Parking mode and what it needs
findings.value: Needs the 70mai Hardwire Kit UP03, sold separately; a collision while parked triggers a 30 s clip
findings.note: Footnote quoted: "The 70mai Hardwire Kit UP03 is required for all parking surveillance functions, sold separately." This is collision-triggered recording, not continuous recording.

findings.label: Storage
